summary.text: Rome ruled lands around the Mediterranean and across much of Europe, Western Asia and North Africa in classical times.
It began when Octavian beat Mark Antony and Cleopatra at Actium in 31 BC, then received the title Augustus in 27 BC as the first emperor.
The Western half collapsed in 476 AD, while the Eastern half, called the Byzantine Empire, lasted until Constantinople fell in 1453.

facts.label: First emperor
facts.value: Octavian became Augustus, the first Roman emperor, in 27 BC

facts.label: Greatest extent
facts.value: Reached its largest size under Trajan, who ruled 98 to 117 AD

facts.label: Western collapse
facts.value: 476 AD, when Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustus

facts.label: Eastern survival
facts.value: The Byzantine Empire lasted until Constantinople fell in 1453

facts.label: Third-century crisis
facts.value: Fifty years of civil war, plagues and invasions

items.prompt: A province in the Roman world belongs to the emperor himself. Who would be running it day to day?
items.explain: Imperial provinces belonged to the emperor and were governed by legates, while senatorial provinces had proconsuls appointed by lot each year.

items.prompt: A Roman general is given an honorary title meaning 'commander'. Which later word of rank comes from that custom?
items.explain: The title imperator was given to successful consuls or generals, and it was always bestowed on the early emperors, which is where the word emperor comes from.

items.prompt: In the years just after 27 BC, Rome still has its Senate and its elected magistrates. Who actually holds all meaningful authority?

options.label: The consuls, who are elected each year
The Senate, which meets as it always did
The man the Senate has just named Augustus

items.explain: The republic stood in name, but Augustus had all meaningful authority after the Senate gave him his new title.

items.prompt: In 476 a Germanic king removes the last emperor in Italy. Where does Roman rule carry on, for roughly another thousand years?

options.label: At Constantinople, in the Eastern Empire
At Palmyra, under its own rulers

items.explain: The Eastern Roman Empire survived with Constantinople as its sole capital until 1453; Ravenna had fallen to the Herulians.

items.prompt: The civil wars of the 3rd century ended with Diocletian's victory. How did he arrange imperial government afterward?

options.label: A single court moved to Byzantium
Two courts, one Greek East and one Latin West
A restored Republic led by the Senate

items.explain: Diocletian set up two different imperial courts in the Greek East and the Latin West; moving the seat to Byzantium came later under Constantine.

items.prompt: Rome's government left a mark on the early United States. Which part of it?

options.label: Rule by emperors from Augustus on

items.explain: Rome's republican institutions influenced medieval Italian city-state republics, the early United States and modern democratic republics.
